extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and appellants handling USPTO appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive criteria governing how applicants and examiners must handle examiner's answers, new grounds of rejection, petitions to designate new grounds, substitute examiner's answers, and reply briefs during USPTO appeals and remands. Focused on timing, permissible content, and consequences of actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of same teachings (different portion of reference) is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board/Examiner reliance on a different portion of the same prior-art reference (e.g., citing an Example instead of an Abstract) does not constitute a new ground of rejection if the portion relied upon "goes no farther than, and merely elaborates upon, what is taught" by the portion previously of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DBC — Board cited an Example on page 16 that elaborated medicinal qualities and preferred orange juice, while the examiner cited the abstract teaching mangosteen rind and fruit/vegetable juice. Because the Example merely elaborated the same two generic limitations fully taught by the abstract, the change was not a new ground. Key point: no new ground if the later-cited portion provides no new teaching beyond what was already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing statutory basis (103 → 102) using same teachings is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer changes the statutory basis of the rejection from 35 U.S.C. 103 to 35 U.S.C. 102 but relies on the same teachings of the remaining reference(s), the change does not constitute a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re May — court affirmed rejection under 102 even though examiner and Board had relied on the same prior-art species when originally rejecting under 103. Rationale: lack of novelty can be the practical equivalent of obviousness when based on the same prior art teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relying on fewer references but same teachings is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer removes one or more references from the statement of rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, but relies on the same teachings of the remaining references as the examiner originally relied upon, that change does not constitute a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Kronig — examiner applied four references, Board limited discussion to three but relied on same teachings; court held no new ground. Key test: whether the basic thrust and teachings relied upon remain the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing order of combined references is not a new ground if teachings identical
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in the stated order of references used in a 35 U.S.C. 103 combination (e.g., citing A in view of B vs B in view of A) is not a new ground of rejection when each reference is cited for the same teaching previously cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Cowles and In re Krammes — different order of combining references did not constitute a new ground because the Board/examiner relied on the same underlying teachings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointing to other portions of an applicant-submitted reference to counter applicant's argument is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant submits a reference and the examiner or Solicitor, in responding to applicant arguments (e.g., 'teaches away'), points to other portions of that same reference to counter the applicant’s argument, this does not constitute a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Hedges — applicant cited portions teaching lower temperatures; Solicitor pointed to other portions showing reactions above claimed temperature. The court held this was not a new ground because the Solicitor merely searched references of record for disclosures pertinent to the same arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for petition to designate a new ground (37 CFR 41.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of the primary examiner's failure to designate a rejection as a new ground in an examiner's answer must be by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 filed within two months from the entry of the examiner's answer and before filing any reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file such a petition constitutes waiver of arguments that a rejection must be designated as a new ground. 37 CFR 41.40 sets the exclusive procedure for review of undesignated new grounds by petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of granted petition: reopening prosecution and two-month reply (37 CFR 41.40(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision granting a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection provides a two-month period in which appellant must file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 to reopen prosecution before the primary examiner; failure to timely file such a reply will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition granted, prosecution reopens and appellant may present amendments, evidence, and/or arguments directed to the new ground; no corrected examiner's answer is provided. Upon filing the reply, the examiner reconsiders and may make the next Office action final (see MPEP § 706.07(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of denied petition: appeal maintained with two-month single reply brief (37 CFR 41.40(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision refusing to grant the petition to designate a new ground provides a two-month period in which appellant may file only a single reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 to maintain the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a reply brief after denial keeps the appeal alive; filing a reply brief after petition but before decision is treated as withdrawal of petition (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of petition by filing reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 is filed within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer and on or after the filing of a petition under 37 CFR 1.181, but before a decision on the petition, the reply brief will be treated as a request to withdraw the petition and to maintain the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a reply brief during pendency of the petition functions as abandonment of the petition and preserves the appeal via reply brief procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for reply periods are limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not applicable to the two-month periods set forth for petitions and replies in 37 CFR 41.40 and related sections; extensions may be available under 37 CFR 1.136(b) for patent applications and 37 CFR 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month statutory reply windows are generally not extendable under the routine 1.136(a) mechanism; practitioners should rely on the limited alternative extension provisions cited when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's options when examiner's answer contains a designated new ground (37 CFR 41.39(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground, appellant must within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer either (1) request that prosecution be reopened before the primary examiner by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (with or without amendment or affidavits or other evidence) or (2) request that the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply requesting reopening will be entered and treated as a request to withdraw the appeal. A reply brief to maintain the appeal must address each new ground of rejection and follow brief requirements; a reply brief cannot be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence (else treated as reopening).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when reopening prosecution in response to a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant requests prosecution be reopened, the reply filed under 37 CFR 1.111 must address each new ground of rejection set forth in the examiner’s answer and may include amendments, affidavits, and/or other evidence relevant to the new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply is not fully responsive but is bona fide, the examiner should provide time for appellant to complete the reply under 37 CFR 1.135(c). If the reply is not bona fide (e.g., does not address the new ground) and the two-month period has expired, the examiner must sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to the affected claims. After a compliant reply is entered, the examiner must reopen prosecution and consider the reply; the examiner may make the next Office action final unless a new ground is introduced that is neither necessitated by applicant amendment nor based on timely-filed IDS information (see MPEP § 706.07(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for reply brief when maintaining appeal in face of new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief to maintain the appeal must address each new ground of rejection as set forth in 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv) and follow the other requirements of a brief set forth in 37 CFR 41.37(c). The reply brief may not include any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply brief should include required items each starting on a separate page (e.g., identification page with appellant’s name, application number, filing date, title, examiner name and art unit, and title 'Reply Brief'; argument pages). Any argument raised in the reply brief that was not raised in the appeal brief, or is not responsive to an argument raised in the examiner’s answer, will not be considered by the Board unless good cause is shown. Jurisdiction passes to the Board upon filing of a reply brief or upon expiration of the time to file it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to timely reply to a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief in response to an examiner's answer that contains a new ground of rejection, the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection. If all claims under appeal are subject, the entire appeal will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners will not normally determine sufficiency of such replies once jurisdiction passes to the Board. If some claims remain, dismissal authorizes cancellation of the affected claims and the appeal continues as to the remaining claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner considerations when reopening prosecution or adding a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to reopen prosecution or to add a new ground of rejection, examiners and supervisors should consider the degree to which the rejection previously of record is being changed, any previous reopenings after the appeal brief, and the overall pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Office action containing a new ground may be made final if the new ground was (A) necessitated by amendment, or (B) based on information presented in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) where no statement under 1.97(e) was filed. Ordinarily, after-final amendments/affidavits/evidence previously refused entry must be entered and considered when reopening prosecution; where multiple conflicting after-final amendments were filed, the first amendment should be entered and subsequent conflicting amendments should not be entered. Form paragraph 12.239 may be used to reopen prosecution and contains suggested wording and bracketed insertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner's answer: appellant options and timing (37 CFR 41.50(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a substitute examiner's answer (e.g., in response to a Board remand for further consideration of a rejection), appellant must within two months from the date of the substitute answer either (i) request reopening of prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment/affidavit/evidence, or (ii) request that the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41. Failure to timely act will result in sua sponte dismissal as to the claims subject to the remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute examiner’s answer may include a new ground of rejection but any new ground must comply with MPEP § 1207.03 requirements. If only some claims are affected, cancellation of those claims is authorized while the appeal continues for others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner's answer responding to remand not for further consideration of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board remands the application to the examiner for a reason other than further consideration of a rejection (e.g., to consider an IDS filed before jurisdiction transferred to the Board, a reply brief raising new issues, an amendment, or an affidavit), the examiner may provide a substitute examiner’s answer; appellant may respond by filing a reply brief within two months from the mailing of the substitute answer, but appellant does not have the option to request reopening prosecution under 37 CFR 41.50(a) unless the remand is for further consideration of a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of any IDS or petition filed while the Board possesses jurisdiction will be held in abeyance until the Board's jurisdiction ends. The two-month reply period is subject to the same extension limits noted earlier (not extendable under 1.136(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval requirements for substitute examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute examiner’s answer prepared in response to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection must be approved by a Technology Center Director (TC Director) or designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 12.285 supplies suggested wording and requires TC Director/designee signature. A substitute examiner’s answer may set forth reasons supporting the rejections and may include new grounds of rejection only if they comply with MPEP § 1207.03.
